# Synthetic fixtures

All files contain disposable test credentials, never personal user data. Copied from the GPL-3.0 KeeForge project; this repository has the same license.

- `keeforge-nul.kdbx`: created by KeeForge at commit 5e3ec2fa0d55 on the test iPhone during issue #181 reproduction. Password `testpassword123`. Successfully saved but strict XML parsing fails because Notes contains literal NUL. This is the end-to-end regression, not a mutation generated by the recovery tool.
- `rich.kdbx`: KeeForge `TestFixtures/kitchen-sink.kdbx`, password `testpassword123`. PyKeePass-generated KDBX 4.1 with attachments, history, protected custom fields, TOTP, custom icons, public custom data, and unknown XML.
- `keyfile.kdbx` / `keyfile.key`: KeeForge `TestFixtures/demo-keyfile.kdbx` / `.key`, password `demo` plus the key file.
- `twofish.kdbx` / `chacha20.kdbx`: KeeForge independent foreign-cipher compatibility fixtures, passwords `foreign-twofish` and `foreign-chacha20` respectively.

Tests inject literal forbidden characters into authenticated plaintext and rebuild the KDBX envelope for synthetic cases. Each expected repaired payload is derived independently and compared byte-for-byte. The real KeeForge reproduction is used unchanged.
- `protected-nul.kdbx`: protected-Notes variant of the same KeeForge iPhone reproduction, password `testpassword123`. Tests decode its protected values independently to prove NUL inside ciphertext is left unchanged.
